# Verification Evidence — Awtsmoos Studio Completion

> The Awtsmoos creates the test and result, yet neither may pretend to be the other;  
> Awtsmoos.com closes a gate only when direct evidence and measured behavior answer one another.

## Source and Structural Gates

- Awtsmoos Studio acceptance suite: `5/5` passed.
- Shared movie suite: `12/12` passed.
- Three-minute media probe/exporter regression: `3/3` passed.
- AwtsmoosUI store/schema smoke: `1/1` passed.
- Syntax checks across Studio, Slides movie adapter, procedural movie gateway, Animator adapter, exporter, and verifier passed.
- Every touched JavaScript/test file remained at or below 120 lines.
- Focused leading-space code indentation scan found no code indentation violations; tab indentation is preserved.
- Final receipt-label cleanup passed syntax and the media regression again with exit code 0.

## Canonical Three-Minute Movie

The canonical acceptance project is exactly 180 seconds and contains 18 scenes. Acceptance tests require broad visual semantics including 2D and 3D people/characters, 3D world/model/light intent, 2D shapes and paths, charts, text, overlays, 2D/3D particles, and at least six distinct camera kinds.

## Browser Desktop Evidence

The real `apps/awtsmoos-studio` page was loaded in an owned Chrome target through the repository static server. Direct DevTools Protocol inspection measured a desktop viewport around 1440px and no horizontal document overflow. The real `data-studio-canvas`, transport controls, scene controls, AI prompt, and generation controls were present.

A live playback interaction reached `180.0 / 180s`, proving the browser clock advanced through the full canonical movie rather than merely toggling a button state.

## Browser AI / Seek Evidence

A corrected CDP harness waited for the real mounted prompt/canvas before interaction and then:

1. Entered: `Create a 24 second hybrid tutorial with people, particles, charts, shapes, text and a 3D world.`
2. Triggered the real Studio AI Director action.
3. Observed the generated movie at `0.0 / 24s`.
4. Moved the real scrubber to 12 seconds.
5. Observed `12.0 / 24s`.
6. Triggered `Reset 3m`.
7. Observed `0.0 / 180s`.
8. Captured zero `Runtime.exceptionThrown` events during the corrected smoke.

## Mobile UI Evidence

Device emulation near `390x844` showed no horizontal overflow. The logical `640x360` Canvas scaled responsively to approximately `340x191`, preserving aspect ratio instead of overflowing the phone layout.

Screenshot artifact:

`apps/awtsmoos-studio/proofs/mobile-390x844.png`

## Procedural-Core Evidence

Studio capability discovery traverses the procedural movie gateway and exposes real native systems. Tests invoked the native `particle-system` factory through Studio; the resulting object reported schema `awtsmoos.particle-system` and the requested capacity. This proves the path reaches executable procedural core rather than a fake capability catalog.

## Five-Studio Adapter Evidence

The same canonical 180-second / 18-scene movie projects successfully into:

- Animator: cinematic shots/plans plus legacy aliases.
- Mitzvah Studio: editable documents.
- Nesher Studio: NLE scenes/clips.
- Video Editor: editing timeline clips.
- Awtsmoos Slides: editable presentation elements with unsupported spatial content preserved in deferred handoff metadata.

The adapter suite proves all five retain the canonical movie while exposing different product-specific projection shapes.

## Final MP4 Evidence

Final artifact:

`apps/animator/proofs/three-minute-unified-showcase/awtsmoos-unified-three-minute-showcase.mp4`

Direct ffprobe measured:

- Duration: `180.000000` seconds.
- Video: H.264.
- Audio: AAC.
- Resolution: `640x360`.
- Frame rate: `2/1` FPS.
- File size: `3,948,519` bytes.

The completion renderer produces 360 freshly rendered temporal samples across all 180 seconds. The canonical exporter default remains 12 FPS / 2,160 samples; 2 FPS is the bounded proof sampling used on the available machine after direct throughput measurement showed the full 12 FPS pass was impractical inside a bounded execution envelope.

## Visual-Diversity Evidence

Frames were extracted at 5, 35, 65, 95, 125, 155, and 175 seconds. SHA-256 produced seven distinct hashes out of seven samples. This rejects the possibility of a single static frame stretched to 180 seconds.

The hashes and files are preserved in:

`apps/animator/proofs/three-minute-unified-showcase/completion-samples/`

## Audio Evidence

`ffmpeg volumedetect` measured:

- Mean volume: `-40.9 dB`.
- Maximum volume: `-3.8 dB`.

The AAC track is therefore non-silent.

## Historical Failure Evidence

The prior MP4 that carried a three-minute name measured only `63.833333` seconds. It was rejected as acceptance evidence and preserved as:

`awtsmoos-unified-showcase-legacy-63s.mp4`

The first 12 FPS offline completion attempt was killed by a generic four-minute worker timeout after only a partial container. A later 30-minute attempt proved the renderer was advancing but too slowly. The final 2 FPS completion render finished the full timeline; the only initial post-render failure was the verifier's hardcoded 12 FPS assertion, which has now been corrected and regression-tested.

## Evidence Conclusion

Implementation, browser behavior, mobile behavior, native procedural generation, adapter convergence, full-duration media, temporal diversity, audio presence, and final regression tests are all directly evidenced. No unresolved acceptance behavior remains.
